title: Governed AI Architecture & Implementation
summary: Design and build AI agents, tools that carry out tasks, and connect them to your systems. Define access, approvals, and how your team will maintain them.
problem: An AI pilot can work in isolation and still fail when it reaches production systems. Access, integration, data boundaries, and ownership need to be designed together.
examine: Applications, workflows, data sources, and existing AI usage
User, application, and agent identities
Limits on connecting systems and responsibilities for running them
change: Define target architecture and approved agent actions
Modernize interfaces and integrate models, tools, and data
Implement access controls, approval points, and operating records
deliver: A map of existing systems and the proposed solution design
An agreed build plan with access rules and safeguards
Working system connections, test results, and maintenance instructions

title: AI Governance Assessment
short: Find the gaps before they spread.
summary: Review the AI tools you use, their access, and who is responsible. Receive prioritized findings and an agreed plan for technical fixes.
problem: Your AI policies may not match what the tools in use can actually access or do. An assessment checks the settings and responsibilities against your requirements.
examine: AI tools, agents, permissions, and data reach
Owners, approvals for putting AI into use, activity records, and review schedules
Existing policies and how they map to configured controls
change: Identify gaps and separate immediate risks from longer-term changes
Name the people responsible for deciding which fixes to make
Define a practical implementation scope
deliver: Findings for company leaders, with the most important issues first
A map of technical safeguards and the observations behind each finding
Priorities for fixes and an agreed next step

title: Agent Governance & Authorization
summary: Specify what each AI agent can read or change, where approval is required, and how its access is reviewed and revoked.
problem: An AI agent can find information or use tools to carry out tasks. You need to know what it is allowed to do, review its access, and remove that access when needed.
examine: Identity and authentication paths for each agent
Tool permissions, delegated access, and resource boundaries
Owner, sponsor, approvals, monitoring, and retirement
change: Limit access and actions to what the agent needs for its task
Require review before consequential actions
Connect access reviews, ownership changes, and offboarding
deliver: A record of each agent, its owner, and its approved access and actions
Configured safeguards and test cases
Responsibilities for reviewing, changing, and removing agent access

title: Microsoft AI Governance
summary: Review how your team uses Copilot and AI agents. Check identities, information access, data protection, and Power Platform settings.
problem: Microsoft AI uses settings across several products. Your team needs to understand how those settings work together to control access, protect information, and assign responsibility.
examine: Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio usage
Entra identities, resource access, and agent lifecycle
Purview controls, Power Platform environments, and integration paths
change: Map relevant controls to actual workloads and licensing
Review source permissions and environment boundaries
Implement and verify the agreed tenant-specific changes
deliver: A map of your Microsoft AI setup and its safeguards
Prioritized configuration and implementation work
Named owners, review requirements, and records to keep

title: AI Integration & Legacy Modernization
summary: Connect AI to older applications through APIs, interfaces that exchange information. Define access, approval steps, and how to handle failures.
problem: Useful business information often sits in older applications and disconnected processes. Connecting AI directly to that information can bypass access rules and make failures harder to handle.
examine: Legacy application interfaces and integration dependencies
Data access patterns, authorization, and failure handling
Hosting, deployment, maintenance, and migration constraints
change: Create APIs with clear rules for information access and permitted actions
Improve system connections and selected parts of older applications
Connect AI features with approval steps and a process for handling unexpected results
deliver: Integration and modernization plan
Tested system connections and working workflows
Migration, recovery, and maintenance guidance

title: Platform Engineering & Technical Operations
short: Build it. Deploy it. Keep it usable.
summary: Build and maintain Next.js websites and applications, their system connections, and release processes. Document how to maintain and recover them.
problem: A platform needs more than a launch. Deployment, content architecture, integrations, maintenance, and recovery must remain understandable as the system changes.
examine: Application architecture, hosting, and deployment process
Content and integration requirements
Performance constraints and ongoing maintenance needs
change: Build or improve Next.js applications and integration layers
Establish reproducible deployment and maintenance workflows
Use AI-assisted development with human review and verification
deliver: Working platform and integration changes
Deployment and recovery documentation
An agreed technical operations scope

title: Governance Remediation & Implementation
summary: Fix the access, identity, activity records, and ongoing management issues found in an assessment. Test the changes and document remaining risks.
problem: An assessment may identify problems your team still needs to fix. Agree on who will make the changes, what the work includes, and how to test that the fixes work.
examine: Assessment findings and affected systems
Dependencies, accountable owners, and change constraints
Current configuration and verification evidence
change: Apply permission, identity, and data-boundary changes
Implement approval, inventory, and lifecycle controls
Update integrations and operating procedures
deliver: Completed changes and test results
An updated map of safeguards and instructions for running the system
Remaining risks and a handover plan
